@ a when~ in a block that is stopped from outside reads the time kept at the last tick of the grid of the body that wrote it: the ticks at 0 2 6 13 read 0 2 6 12, so the part runs at the tick 13 too
process 0 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
process 1 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
process 2 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
@ a reset_if~ in a block that is stopped from outside reads the same time: the part is put back at the ticks 0 6 13, and the ticks 2 does not
process 0 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
process 1 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
process 2 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
- two when~ outside the block stop it where both hold: the grid counts the frames of c1 && c2, so the part is the one of V
- a reset_if~ outside the block that comes between the runs of a tick that runs: the tick at the frame 13 reads the time 12 and runs, and the reset at the frame 14 takes back what it dealt
@ a block of 4: the grid of the part counts 4 runs a tick, the ticks are the runs 0 and 4 (the frames 0 and 6) and the time kept at the frame 6 is 4, so the second tick does not run

process 1 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
@ a block inside a block reads the same time: the outer pair and the inner block tick together every 2 runs, so the vector is V
